text:
eva_marketing: Quick ask from marketing for the launch post + webinar: we need the canonical benchmark artifacts and a compact methodology blurb. Can runtime export the run that produced the numbers we discussed?

Need list:
- latency CDFs (p50/p90/p95/p99) for baseline float32 and two quantized configs (q8_0, q4_1)
- steady-state traces (exclude warmup) and raw_payloads.json.gz (anonymized seeds)
- exact repro steps: docker image + sha, model file checksum, full env.txt, and the CLI used to invoke the bench
- warmup details: how many warmup requests, whether warmup was parallel, and how we measured steady-state start
- batch/concurrency config and any continuous-batching knobs that were on/off
- a one-paragraph README describing methodology we can paste into the blog/webinar notes (tokens per request, sampling vs greedy, rng seed if used)

Deadline: EOD Thursday if possible. Small legal will want the methodology line, and comms will want a one-sentence caveat about warmup and tail behavior. :eyes:

josh_runtime: Got it. A few clarifying Qs: do you want CDFs that include cold-start spikes or strictly steady-state? And do you need token-level content in traces or can we send timing-only traces with prompts redacted?

eva_marketing: Steady-state only (remove the first 30s from plots). Traces: timing + token lengths are fine but redact prompt text. We can use the seed list you provide to run synthetic content for demos.

micaela_sre: Note retention: detailed traces are rotated after 7 days. If you want preserved artifacts, we need to export to perf-bench-exports S3. I can bump retention for this run if you ask now. Also: perf-ci-bot can snapshot CPU/GPU profiles and upload flamegraphs.

josh_runtime: We'll schedule a deterministic rerun on dedicated nodes to ensure clean steady-state numbers. Plan: fixed RNG, continuous batching ON, target_batch=16, concurrency=8, 30s warmup, sample_length=256 tokens, request rate ramp over 60s then steady for 5m. We'll produce: traces-2067890123.tar.gz, raw_payloads-2067890123.json.gz, env-2067890123.txt, run_config-2067890123.json, and README-methodology-2067890123.md. ETA ~36h.

perf-ci-bot: Export for run 2067890123 queued. On upload the S3 URI will be posted here.

eva_marketing: Perfect. Can you include a tiny snippet we can embed in the blog showing the exact curl command you used to run the bench (so readers can reproduce)? Even one-liner is fine.

josh_runtime: Sure, we'll include a reproducibility snippet. Example we'll provide: 

curl -X POST https://runtime.internal/api/v1/bench/run \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RUNTIME_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","batch":16,"concurrency":8,"seed":42}'

Also note: quantized runs use q8_0 conversion pipeline; we will attach the model conversion hash and the quant tool version.

micaela_sre: If marketing needs the artifacts uploaded sooner I can prioritize the job on the dedicated pool; DM me.

eva_marketing: Thanks all 60a We'll review as soon as the upload appears and flag anything that needs follow-up.
